reviewer: Codex (AI agent), not a human reviewer
scope: Manual semantic comparison of two accepted live explanations against original synthetic development snapshots and the single top policy supplied to synthesis. Outputs preserved exactly.
automatedAcceptance: The end-to-end script passed 17 engineering checks; that does not establish semantic correctness.
limitations: This is an AI-assisted review of two selected synthetic development cases, not independent human adjudication or a real-world accuracy estimate.

The model saw a compact authoritative assessment and tool evidence IDs, not the complete tool output in its synthesis prompt; the reviewer separately inspected the checkpointed complete operational evidence.
Later review decisions do not retroactively justify text that described an action as completed when the investigation was generated.

citations.title: Transport timeout after processing
citations.excerpt: A client transport timeout does not establish payment failure. Correlate the accepted request, idempotency key and processor payment reference. A SUCCEEDED processor confirmation plus exactly one matching capture ledger entry establishes completed capture for this simulated workflow. Reconcile the amount and currency before proposing case resolution. Explain that retrying without checking the original reference can create ambiguity. Never propose a second debit or an automatic refund from a timeout alone. If confirmation or matching ledger evidence is absent, request evidence instead.

citations.title: Refund posting and payout reconciliation
citations.excerpt: All values are integer minor units in a single currency. Compute ledger net as the signed sum of capture, fee and refund postings. For a succeeded payment, expected processor payout equals capture amount minus processor fee minus confirmed refunds. A confirmed processor refund that is absent from the ledger creates a difference equal to that refund when other postings agree. Preserve the processor refund reference, confirmation event, ledger snapshot cutoff and exact difference. Escalate the posting exception for a human reconciliation review. The investigator must not create a refund, repair a ledger or transfer money.

citations.title: Human review of case proposals
citations.excerpt: An investigator proposes RESOLVE_CASE, ESCALATE or REQUEST_EVIDENCE. Only a reviewer distinct from the investigation creator can approve or reject a stored proposal. Apply the stored proposal, check the current case version, and persist the decision and audit entry atomically. Reusing an idempotency key with the same request returns the original decision; a different request with that key must conflict. These actions change case workflow only and never change a payment.

warnings: Synthetic data only; proposals change case disposition, never payment or ledger balances.

supportedClaims.claim: Provider success and exactly one matching ledger capture establish observed successful capture in this simulated policy.

issues.explanation: At generation the stored result status is AWAITING_REVIEW and action RESOLVE_CASE is only a proposal. The operational snapshot proves payment capture, not execution of a case-review command. The supplied policy says to propose resolution; it does not authorize the model to declare the case already resolved.
An independent review is still required for case disposition. The phrase could be defensible only if explicitly limited to an additional financial operation, which the generated text does not do.

minorObservations: The same policy citation ID is repeated twice in the finding. Its identity is valid; the duplicate adds no support.
